title: Relative degreewise pseudo-coherence over a finite type algebra
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings, let $R\to A$ be of finite type, meaning that $A$ is generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra, let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $M\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Say that $M$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$ if there exist $n\geq0$ and a surjective $R$-algebra map $\alpha:P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $\operatorname{Res}_\alpha M\in D(P)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. Here $\operatorname{Res}_\alpha$ is the ordinary-module derived restriction of scalars [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension], induced by applying restriction of scalars termwise to a representing complex: additive groups and differentials are unchanged and $p$ acts as $\alpha(p)$. On module categories restriction is additive and exact: kernels and cokernels have their original additive groups with the restricted action. Its termwise functor therefore induces the displayed functor on derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].
